evidence.approach: A pnpm workspace with turborepo driving four tasks across six packages. The mechanism that matters: each library package declares main and types as ./src/index.ts and is depended on as workspace:*, tsconfig.base.json maps @seen/* to packages/*/src, apps/api and apps/worker compile with tsc over a project rooted at the repository root so the packages' sources land in the app's own dist, and apps/web sets transpilePackages so Next.js compiles the same sources. The library packages have no build script at all, so there is nothing to publish and one change to the trade record lands in one commit. turbo's build task depends on ^build and outputs dist and .next; test, lint and typecheck have no dependencies and parallelise. Vitest runs in the node environment everywhere. Redis for the worker is the local server here and a service container in CI, read from the environment either way.
changes: package.json: private workspace root, packageManager pnpm@10.31.0, engines node >=24, scripts delegating to turbo
pnpm-workspace.yaml and turbo.json: the six packages and the four tasks with their dependsOn and outputs
tsconfig.base.json: strict TypeScript, ES2023, node module resolution and the @seen/* path mapping
eslint.config.mjs: one flat config for the repository, typescript-eslint recommended
.nvmrc: 24.15.0, restoring what the Seene removal deleted
packages/core, packages/connectors, packages/agent: package.json with main and types on src/index.ts and no build script, tsconfig.json, src/index.ts, src/index.test.ts, vitest.config.ts
apps/api: main.ts, app.module.ts, health.controller.ts answering GET /health, health.test.ts through the Nest testing module and supertest, tsconfig rooted at the repository root
apps/worker: main.ts, the hello queue and its worker, hello.test.ts enqueuing a job and awaiting completion against Redis
apps/web: next.config.ts with transpilePackages, app/layout.tsx, app/page.tsx, site.ts and site.test.ts
.github/workflows/ci.yml: a node job for lint, typecheck, test and build with a Redis service container, beside the harness and graph jobs
tests_first: packages/*/src/index.test.ts asserts each package's exported name, proving it resolves, compiles and runs under Vitest: the RED must fail because no package.json exists and pnpm has nothing to run
apps/api health.test.ts expects GET /health to answer 200 with a status body: the RED must fail because there is no module to bootstrap
apps/worker hello.test.ts enqueues a hello job and waits for the worker to complete it against Redis: the RED must fail because the queue and its processor do not exist
apps/web metadata.test.ts asserts the site title the layout exports: the RED must fail because the module does not exist
alternatives: npm or yarn workspaces, rejected because the ground rules name pnpm and the lockfile discipline in CI depends on it
Nx instead of turborepo, rejected for the same reason and because turbo's task graph is enough for four tasks
Building the library packages to dist and consuming the output, rejected by the ticket: plain TypeScript compiled by the consumer is what keeps one schema change to one commit
Docker Compose for Redis in the worker test, rejected because the daemon is not running on this machine and a service container covers CI
risks: Install time and cold build could exceed the five-minute criterion; mitigated by keeping dependencies minimal and by timing the run and recording it
Next.js and NestJS pull large dependency trees, so a supply-chain audit matters; SEEN-089 adds pnpm audit at high and SEEN-090 the rest
The worker test needs Redis and will fail where there is none; mitigated by reading host and port from the environment and by CI declaring the service
tsc compiling package sources into each app's dist means the same source is compiled more than once; accepted, because it is what keeps the packages publish-free, and turbo caches it
evidence.rollback: Revert the commit. Nothing outside the repository changes, no database is touched and no credential is used.
new_dependencies: turbo, typescript, vitest, eslint, typescript-eslint, @types/node at the root
